national.line: A Tennessee gymnast held a knuckle handstand for a record-breaking 1 minute, 23 seconds after more than four months of training. Talk about knuckling down.
A Nebraska woman got back the wedding ring she lost at a University of Nebraska-Lincoln football game, thanks to a friend and a news article. Now that's a Husker happy ending.
The Gateway Arch in St. Louis was completed 61 years ago today, and at 630 feet it is the tallest monument in the Western Hemisphere. Tall order, nailed it.
Etsy is cracking down on AI-generated content to protect buyers and its nearly 6 million handmade sellers from a flood of AI slop. Handmade just got a bodyguard.
The Minnesota Zoo welcomed three orphaned brown bear cubs rescued in Alaska. Now they've got the bear necessities.
A woman dug up and opened a time capsule her great-grandfather buried in his front yard in 1976, and she never met him. Best late delivery ever.

pride.label: Navy Scholarship
pride.line: Chapel Banner, a Bolivar High School senior, won a four-year Navy ROTC scholarship that covers full college tuition, one of only about 100 students picked nationwide this way this year. The Navy knows talent when it sees it.

pride.label: Life Saving Award
pride.line: Eight people received Lebanon's Life Saving Award on Oct. 26 for saving a Missouri Cooperage worker who collapsed from a cardiac event on July 8: coworker Tyler Blattel, Lt. Joe Gerber, Capt. Terry Saltzman, firefighters Adam Moppin, Nick Davis and Paul Shomo, paramedic Louis Corbeil and EMT Jeremy Vinson. Now that's teamwork.

pride.label: Apprenticeship
pride.line: Julia Jones of Bolivar finished her Dental Assistant Registered Apprenticeship at the OCHC Bolivar clinic through the district's BoMo Works program, and plans to become a dental hygienist. She's off to a spotless start.

pride.label: District Champs
pride.line: Bolivar softball won the district championship, beating Aurora 12-2 as the one seed, then reached the state quarterfinal on Oct. 24. That's how you earn a one seed.

local.line: Lebanon residents in Wards 1 and 4 hauled roughly 200 cars' worth of cleanup to Level Up Lebanon this fall, the program's biggest season yet. That's a lot of junk with nowhere left to hide.

The Missouri Department of Natural Resources gave Camden County Public Water Supply District No. 5 a $223,000 interest-free loan on Oct. 27 for drinking water planning, saving ratepayers about $48,000 in interest. Free money for clean water.
Osage Beach's Highway 42 sidewalk is switching to the other side of the road, and that move may finally get it built. Sidewalk plans, finally stepping forward.
A Lake of the Ozarks resort owner plans to buy and renovate the foreclosed Regalia Hotel in Lake Ozark, which has been eerily quiet this year. Lights on again soon.
The Webster County Health Unit officially launched its Baby Bridge program to help families with babies and toddlers at all stages, after a two-month pilot. Little ones, big support.

music.line: Cody Johnson brought out Parker McCollum to sing 'Good Time Charlie's Got the Blues' at his London show. Country goes international.
Carly Pearce sang the national anthem before Game 3 of the World Series, and fans praised her strong, rich vocals. Home run of a performance.
Garth Brooks announced two Hamilton, Ontario concerts at TD Coliseum in December, his first Canadian stop on the Blame It All On My Roots tour. Friends in cold places.
George Strait gave a rare speech as he received the Career Maker Award, and Taylor Swift and Lyle Lovett joined the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame. The King still has the floor.
NBC will air a special broadcast of Alan Jackson's final concert in December, from the Last Call: One More For the Road finale. Set your DVR to country.
Country star Terri Clark says her band thinks she needs therapy for her fishing addiction. Tell them it's a reel problem.
Riley Green had an 'extremely difficult' call choosing between Cade Mower and Brayden Howell in a Battle round on The Voice. Never an easy chair to turn.
Eric Church released a reflective new single called 'On The Road.' Pack a playlist.
Walker Montgomery married Tigirlily Gold's Krista Slaubaugh, with handwritten vows over morning coffee and a George Strait classic. Now that's a country wedding.
Country star Chris Young signed with United Talent Agency. New chapter, same great voice.

weird.line: Raising Cane's founder Todd Graves brought a 3,156-pound pumpkin to Salem, Massachusetts, and left with a new Guinness World Record. That's one jumbo order.
The Los Angeles Public Library is hosting the world's largest pop-up book as part of its centennial celebration. Finally, a book you can't skim.
A pet groomer YouTuber went viral after a goat turned out to be her 'dream client.' Finally, a client who kids around.
An emu was spotted on the loose among traffic in Lancaster. Somebody forgot to tell it the speed limit.
A live deer sitting inside a car in Buffalo, New York, has gone viral. Hope it buckled up.
A Florida woman says a neighbor complained that her Halloween decorations were too scary, and wouldn't walk on their sidewalk. Mission accomplished, then.
An angler caught a record-breaking channel catfish near Pittsburgh, topping the mark set in 1991. That's a whisker above the rest.
A Minnesota grower travelled 35 hours with a 2,389-pound pumpkin and won California's weigh-off. That's one well-traveled pumpkin.
A dinosaur fossil found in Montana sold for $47.3 million at auction. Talk about a dino-mite price.
In North Dakota, a pet snake turned up in the wrong house, then rode to the pound in a toy cruiser. Slithering in style.
A 76-foot smoker from Justin set a Guinness World Record as the largest food truck. That's a lot of brisket real estate.
Comedian Shane Gillis set two Guinness World Records at a sold-out Philadelphia stadium show. He really brought the house down.
A Florida woman in a banana costume reported a car accident, and the call was so strange it prompted the question, 'Is this AI?' Peel back the details.
Texas firefighters used the Jaws of Life to free a raccoon with its head stuck in a tree. Best rescue of the week.
Hazmat crews removed a mysterious cylinder that washed ashore on a beach in Flagler County, Florida, after storms. The ocean's way of sending a package.
A strange sphere was spotted over Joplin, Missouri. Joplin gets visitors too.
Brooklyn artist Olivia Springberg made a giant Halloween 'Pizza Rat' sculpture crawling down a townhouse in New York's West Village. Rent's high, but that rat's staying.
A young miniature donkey named Rodney snuggled with his favorite human as part of his training at Sunflower Farm Creamery in Cumberland, Maine. Best training session ever.
A bowhunter in Georgia took a buck that could be a new record-class deer. That's a rack worth bragging about.
Scientists found a 160-million-year-old 'squid' so fat it broke every record, and only two fossils exist. Talk about a heavy hitter.

humor.line: The word chocolate comes from the Aztec word xocolatl, which means 'bitter water.' Bitter water never tasted so good.
You can even order a plush version of your real-life pet. Finally, a pet that never sheds.
The Statue of Liberty arrived in New York in 214 packing crates in 1885. Talk about assembly required.
Emile Reynaud's Theatre Optique showed the first public projected moving images in 1892. Saturday mornings owe him one.
Wild-food enthusiast Euell Gibbons and his 1962 book, Stalking the Wild Asparagus, may have inspired the day. Grocery aisle not included.
The first electronic message between computers was sent in 1969 over ARPANET, linking UCLA, Stanford and two other schools. No cat videos yet, sadly.
Domestic cats are thought to descend from the Middle Eastern wildcat, tamed about 12,000 years ago, and 90 million house cats now live in the U.S. They still think they own the place.
Steel-cut oats are sliced with steel blades, while rolled oats are steamed and flattened. Either way, it sticks to your ribs.
The first American doughnuts were little 'nuts' of dough brought to New England by the Pilgrims, who learned the recipe in Holland. A hole lot of history.
Breadsticks began in Turin, Italy, in the 1600s, and legend credits Antonio Brunero of the Savoy Court. Legend says he knew his bread.
Candy corn is made from sugar, corn syrup and confectioner's wax. Yes, there's wax in it.
Caution is thrown to the wind and texts to exes get sent, though the day also suggests reflecting on past relationships instead. Maybe just text your mom.
It lands less than a week after National Pumpkin Day, so there's often an extra pumpkin sitting around. Leftover pumpkin finally has a job.
Scientists think lemurs floated to Madagascar on vegetation from Africa's mainland. Talk about a free ride.
Jack-o'-lantern carving started with turnips in Ireland and Britain, tied to the story of Stingy Jack. Imagine a turnip on your porch.
A San Jose woman started handing out books instead of candy in 1995 because candy was the main Halloween treat. Kids got a plot twist with their trick-or-treat.
It's a day for adults handing out candy to sneak some for themselves before trick-or-treaters arrive. Call it quality control.
The Halloween & Costume Association created it in 2019 after a petition to move Halloween to the last Saturday of October. Halloween negotiations went surprisingly well.
Some believe knock-knock jokes came from guards in the Middle Ages checking who showed up at the castle after dark. Who's there? Nobody knows.
It began in Philadelphia in 1950, when kids collected coins in decorated milk cartons and raised $17 for UNICEF. Small change, big start.
Candy maker William Kolb made an early candy apple in Newark, New Jersey, in 1908 while experimenting with red cinnamon candy. A happy accident worth biting into.
Author Nancy Christie says we should use the extra hour from Daylight Saving Time ending to rest instead of work. Permission to do nothing, granted.
McCormick created it in 2019 to kick off what the spice company calls Cinnamon Season. Of course the spice company did.
Calzone translates to 'trousers' or 'pants legs,' and it began as a street food for workers in Naples. So it's basically pizza wearing pants.
In 1884, 25 nations met in Washington, D.C., to choose Greenwich, England, as zero longitude. Even the map had to take a vote.
A woman's club president in Illinois thought it up in 1928 to thank her favorite author. Best fan letter ever written.
Vinegar is used for pickling, cleaning, gardening and pest control. It's the multitool of the kitchen.
Cookie Monster got his start in 1966, three years before debuting on Sesame Street. Me want birthday cookie.
It marks the first commercial radio broadcast, on Pittsburgh's KDKA in 1920, which happened to be election night. Somebody had to schedule the spots.
Deviled eggs are also called eggs mimosa, stuffed eggs and dressed eggs. Every potluck needs the egg tray.
It's a day for kids learning shapes to find circles up, down and every which way. Your steering wheel counts.
The whole point is to use clichés as much as possible, and one page lists 681 of them. That's the way the cookie crumbles.
Give a dollar to someone you know, a stranger, or a charity. A dollar still goes somewhere.
It's the birthday of John Montagu, the fourth Earl of Sandwich, born in 1718. He really named the lunch.
Jellyfish are about 95 percent water, and they aren't actually fish. Basically wet, wobbly water.
